channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Passenger Train Collides with Truck in Kazakhstan's Karaganda Region
item.description: A passenger train and a truck collided at an unregulated railway crossing in the Shet district of Kazakhstan's Karaganda region. The truck driver reportedly failed to ensure the safety of passage, but no injuries were reported.

item.title: Israel Restricts Palestinian Workers' Entry to West Bank Ahead of Elections
item.description: The Israeli military announced that Palestinian workers with permits will be barred from entering Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank on Sunday and Monday. Restrictions also apply to industrial zones. On election day, all entry and exit from the West Bank and Jordan Valley will be blocked, with land crossings closed. Settlers have also reportedly prevented farmers from harvesting olives.

item.title: Over 400,000 Protest Across France Against Cost of Living and Nationalism
item.description: At least 410,000 people participated in protests across France on October 24, according to the Interior Ministry. Unions reported up to 800,000 attendees. Protesters voiced anger over inflation, high fuel prices, poor public services, and wealth inequality. Clashes with police occurred in several cities, including Paris, leading to arrests.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Economy Shows Strong Growth, Exceeding Regional Averages
item.description: Kazakhstan's economy has grown by approximately 30% since 2019, averaging about 4.5% annually, a respectable pace for a developing nation. GDP per capita has surpassed $15,000 nominally, with purchasing power parity estimates around $35-40,000. Life expectancy has reached nearly 76 years, the best in the region. The country has advanced its automotive and rail industries from minimal localization to full-cycle production.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Suspected of Assaulting Taxi Driver in South Korea
item.description: An Uzbek citizen is suspected of assaulting a taxi driver in Hwaseong city, South Korea. The suspect allegedly attacked the driver who was attempting to film his illegal taxi service. The 50-year-old Korean victim lost consciousness after the assault.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Reviews Socio-Economic Development in Chatkal District
item.description: The President of Kyrgyzstan visited the Chatkal district in Jalal-Abad region to review its socio-economic development, implemented projects, and future plans. Investments totaling 20.6 billion soms were made between 2021 and September 2026. Tax revenue targets were met, and healthcare and education indicators improved.

item.title: Elon Musk Accuses Ukraine of Using Starlink for Attacks Aimed at Killing People
item.description: Elon Musk accused Ukraine's armed forces of using Starlink for offensive attacks intended to kill people, stating the loophole was closed last week. He confirmed SpaceX had limited Starlink's speed in Ukraine, emphasizing its crucial role in Ukraine's defense while criticizing 'hypocritical war-mongers'.

item.title: Protesters and Police Clash in Brussels During Anti-Government Demonstration
item.description: Belgian police used tear gas and pepper spray against protesters in Brussels who chanted anti-government slogans and demanded improvements to the education system. Clashes occurred after hundreds gathered for ongoing demonstrations. Police stated that measures were taken to ensure public order and safety.

item.title: Tariffs Could Help End Five Wars, Assesses Trump on Potential 200% Duties on Russian and Ukrainian Goods
item.description: US President Donald Trump suggested that tariffs could help end five wars. He evaluated the possibility of imposing 200% duties on goods from Russia and Ukraine.

item.title: President Japarov Comments on Alexey Shirshov's Role and State Asset Recovery
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov addressed the role of Alexey Shirshov, stating that politicians use Shirshov's name for criticism. He confirmed Shirshov's past involvement in energy system management and alleged corruption, detailing how information provided by Shirshov helped recover state assets worth approximately $20 million.

item.title: Direct Air Service Launched Between Astana and Oman
item.description: Air Astana has operated its inaugural flight on the Astana-Salalah route. The flight carried 140 passengers to Oman. Flights will be operated by Airbus A320 aircraft. This new route aims to develop tourism, trade, economic, and cultural ties between Kazakhstan and Oman.

item.title: Nurlan Orazalin Recounts Heated Debate During Adoption of Sovereignty Declaration
item.description: Nurlan Orazalin, a deputy of the 12th convocation of the Supreme Council of the Kazakh SSR, described the adoption of the Declaration of State Sovereignty as a complex and crucial period. He recalled a heated debate lasting seven hours, with 18 deputies voting against it.

item.title: Trump Considers Military Strike on Iran or a Diplomatic Deal
item.description: US President Donald Trump stated that a military strike on Iran could occur soon, but an agreement with Tehran also remains a possibility. He indicated the US was weighing the option of an attack while a major deal was also on the table. Trump expressed confidence in his handling of Iran, suggesting he might "finish the job" or Iran could agree to a deal, asserting the US would "win either way."

item.title: New 265-Bed Oncology Center to Be Built in Tashkent
item.description: A new 265-bed oncology center will be constructed in Tashkent as part of a medical cluster being established in collaboration with the Korean Eximbank. A contract for consulting services has been signed with a South Korean company for the project. The center will be built within the medical cluster.

item.title: Obama: We Prevented Iran from Obtaining Nuclear Weapons Through Diplomacy
item.description: Former US President Barack Obama stated that his administration prevented Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons through diplomatic means, without resorting to military action. He emphasized the success of diplomacy in achieving this objective, highlighting that no missiles were fired.

item.title: France Sees Renewed Protests Against Rising Cost of Living
item.description: Mass protests against the rising cost of living have resumed in France, with over 800,000 people participating nationwide. Clashes between police and demonstrators occurred in Paris, where authorities used water cannons and tear gas. Similar incidents were reported in other major cities. Organizers claim 800,000 participated, while authorities estimate 410,000.

item.title: Global Wheat Prices Drop 12% in One Month Amid Improved Harvest Outlook
item.description: Global wheat prices have fallen by approximately 12% over the past month, reaching $229 per ton on the US exchange. Experts attribute the decline to improved harvest expectations for the current season. Major exporters like Russia and Ukraine are increasing shipments, influencing both global and domestic prices.

item.title: Kazakhstan Begins Implementing Military Reform to Create Modern, Agile Army
item.description: Kazakhstan has commenced the implementation of a military reform plan, approved by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, aiming to establish a modern, agile, and technologically advanced army. The reform focuses on enhancing military service safety, command culture, and efficient resource utilization.

item.title: Taliban Official Urges Takhar University Students to Practice Religion
item.description: A Taliban official responsible for Invitation and Guidance at Takhar University has reportedly urged students to practice their religion. Some students alleged the official described them as "irreligious." The meeting also reportedly discussed clothing and beard styles, reflecting the Taliban's efforts to impose their interpretation of religious practice on society.

item.title: Kazakhstan Celebrates Republic Day After 13-Year Hiatus
item.description: Kazakhstan is celebrating Republic Day on October 25, a national holiday marked by cultural and sporting events. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated Kazakhstan has become a respected, influential middle power. This is the fifth time Republic Day is celebrated since its re-establishment in 2022.

item.title: France Sees Mass Protests with Nearly a Thousand Arrests and Serious Injuries
item.description: France experienced widespread protests on October 24th against the rising cost of living, cuts to public services, and social inequality. Despite official bans and heavy security, hundreds of thousands participated. In several cities, peaceful marches escalated into clashes with police, resulting in arrests and injuries. Unions have announced further protest dates.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Introduce Mandatory Deposit System for Plastic and Glass Bottles
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering a mandatory deposit system for empty plastic and glass bottles, and aluminum cans. The proposal aims to incentivize separate waste collection and increase recycling rates, which currently stand at only 6.2%. The system would involve a refundable deposit added to the product price.

item.title: Kazakhstan Restores Republic Day as National Holiday
item.description: Kazakhstan has reinstated Republic Day, celebrated on October 25, as a national holiday. The day commemorates the adoption of the Declaration of State Sovereignty in 1990, a pivotal step towards independence. President Tokayev proposed restoring the holiday's status in July 2022.

item.title: Two New Cotton Processing Plants Open in Turkistan Region
item.description: Two additional cotton processing plants have been launched in the Syrdariya settlement of the Otyrar district, Turkistan region, as part of efforts to develop cotton farming and deepen agricultural product processing. This brings the total operational plants for the "Turkistan Tekstil" company to four. The opening ceremony was attended by the regional governor, who highlighted the importance of such projects for boosting industrial potential.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Increase Social Benefits and Pensions from 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will increase social benefits, certain pensions, and monetary compensations starting January 1, 2027. The most significant increase is planned for people with disabilities. Other categories, including children who lost parents, Hero Mothers, WWII veterans, donors, and Chernobyl liquidators, will also see an increase. President Sadyr Japarov also ordered a three-month rent exemption for traders relocating from the 'Madina' market.

item.title: Pakistan Media Covers Uzbekistan's International Summit on Child Wellbeing
item.description: Pakistan's Associated Press of Pakistan (APP) reported on the International Summit 'Investing in Child Wellbeing: Towards Sustainable and Equitable Development for Future Generations' held in Samarkand. The summit, organized by Uzbekistan with UN and World Bank collaboration, focused on child protection, education, healthcare, and investment. The Samarkand Declaration outlined strategic goals for child welfare.

item.title: Conference Explores Central Asia-Asia-Pacific Connectivity and Cooperation
item.description: A conference in Vladivostok discussed new levels of connectivity between Central Asia and the Asia-Pacific region. Scholars and experts from various countries, including Central Asia, China, Japan, and Korea, participated. Uzbekistan's representative highlighted the region's shift towards strategic alignment and economic cooperation, driven by political trust among leaders.

item.title: US Intelligence Warns of Increased Iranian Threats in Middle East
item.description: US intelligence reports an increase in Iranian agents' activities abroad, including potential threats against American officials and diplomats even within the United States. The head of US intelligence highlighted the heightened risk, emphasizing the growing Iranian focus on targeting Americans in the Middle East.

item.title: Afghanistan Reports Rising Polio Cases, Including Young Child's Paralysis
item.description: Afghanistan faces a surge in polio cases, with 42 recorded in the first 10 months of 2026, double last year's figures. Five-year-old Zahra from Baghlan province is among those paralyzed by the disease due to lack of vaccine availability. Afghanistan and Pakistan remain the only countries where wild poliovirus has not been eradicated.

item.title: Uzbekistan Energy Minister Reviews Progress on Solar Power and Energy Storage Project
item.description: Uzbekistan's Energy Minister Sherzod Khodjaev inspected the construction of a solar power plant and energy storage system in Nurabad district, Samarkand region. The project, a collaboration with Saudi company ACWA, aims for a 1000 MW solar capacity and a 1336 MW·h storage system. The first 100 MW phase is operational, with full completion expected by the end of 2027.

item.title: Afghan Citizens and Activists Protest Forced Deportations in Germany
item.description: Afghan citizens and civil society activists in Germany have protested against the forced deportation of asylum seekers, particularly to Afghanistan. Demonstrations occurred in several German cities and airports, with protesters calling for an end to deportations, opposing expanded detention facilities, and urging Germany to uphold the right to asylum.

item.title: US Administrations Urged SpaceX to Modify Starlink Use in Conflicts
item.description: Both the Biden and Trump administrations repeatedly asked Elon Musk to alter Starlink's operations in Ukraine and the Middle East. US presidents relied heavily on the private company for foreign policy implementation during various conflicts.

item.title: France Sees Large Protests with Approximately 800,000 Participants
item.description: An estimated 800,000 people took to the streets in France today as part of a new wave of protests. The demonstrations indicate a significant level of public mobilization and discontent.

item.title: Switzerland Spent Over $16,000 Hosting Taliban Delegation for Deportation Talks
item.description: Switzerland spent more than $16,000 to host a Taliban delegation in Geneva in August 2025. The purpose was to identify Afghan citizens convicted of crimes in Switzerland for deportation. Documents show Swiss officials shared personal information, raising safety concerns for deportees.

item.title: Charlie Chaplin's Legacy Unites Filmmakers in Tashkent Event
item.description: Tashkent hosted a special international event celebrating the cinematic achievements of Central Asian and Caucasian countries, centered around the legacy of Charlie Chaplin. The program included a press conference, the Chaplin Awards ceremony, and a film screening, supported by the Ministry of Culture of Uzbekistan. The event fostered discussions on international cooperation in cinema.

item.title: Two More Cotton Processing Plants Launched in Turkestan Region
item.description: Two additional cotton processing plants, operated by "Turkistan Tokyma" LLP, have been launched in the Syrdaria settlement of the Otyrar district, Turkestan Region. This brings the company's total number of plants to four. The launch ceremony was attended by the regional governor, who highlighted the importance of agricultural product processing and value-added production.

item.title: Afghan Envoy to Switzerland Highlights UN Missions' Role in Defending Rights
item.description: Afghanistan's ambassador to Switzerland, Nasir Ahmad Andisha, stated that diplomatic missions at the UN are actively defending people's rights, especially for women and girls, and upholding international commitments. He emphasized the UN as a bastion for defending charter values against the erosion of rights under Taliban rule.

item.title: Yemen War: Houthi Claim 16 Killed in Saudi Airstrikes
item.description: The Houthi group claims that 16 people were killed in Saudi airstrikes in Yemen. This statement comes amidst the ongoing conflict and highlights the continued violence in the region.

item.title: Reed Fire Extinguished on Shore of Kapchagay Reservoir in Almaty Region
item.description: A fire in the reeds on the shore of the Kapchagay Reservoir, near Alatau city in Kazakhstan's Almaty Region, was being fought on October 24. Firefighters faced difficulties due to difficult terrain, limited access for special vehicles, wind, and approaching darkness.

item.title: UAE Closes Beaches and Coastal Areas Due to Oil Spill
item.description: All beaches and coastal areas in the Umm Al Quwain emirate of the UAE have been temporarily closed due to an oil spill from a tanker. The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment reported the incident, stating cleanup operations have begun. Residents in Sharjah and Ajman reported a foul odor.
